skill.name: lark-skill-maker
skill.description: Create reusable Lark CLI skills that wrap Lark APIs, shortcuts, and multi-step office workflows.
skill.summary: Guides agents through designing reusable Lark CLI skills with API research, templates, scopes, and safety checks.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged Markdown backticks, sibling-skill links, a placeholder workflow comment, and a high-entropy heuristic in SKILL.md. Manual review found readable documentation for creating Lark CLI skills, with no prompt injection, obfuscated payload, or hidden executable script. The skill still depends on authenticated lark-cli operations, so write actions should continue to require explicit user confirmation and minimal scopes.

remediation.issue: Command examples can perform authenticated Lark writes when users adapt generated skills.
remediation.suggestion: Keep explicit confirmation, scope review, and dry-run guidance for POST, PATCH, DELETE, and shortcut write operations.

remediation.issue: Sibling skill references use parent-directory Markdown links that can trigger path traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Use marketplace skill identifiers when available, or clearly state that the links only point to bundled sibling skills.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 uses inline Markdown around the filename SKILL.md. It is documentation text, not Ruby backtick execution or shell evaluation.
Line 16 opens a Markdown bash code fence for lark-cli examples. The skill does not contain executable Ruby backticks or an automatic shell invocation.
Line 21 closes a Markdown code fence. It has no command execution behavior by itself.
Line 23 uses inline Markdown formatting around the word api. This is prose about command priority, not a shell execution primitive.
Line 27 opens a Markdown bash example block for API research commands. The commands are documented examples for the declared lark-cli tool, not hidden executable code.
Line 37 closes the Markdown code block that started on line 27. It does not execute or evaluate shell content.
Line 39 references a sibling skill and formats lark-cli api as inline Markdown. This is expected documentation for Lark OpenAPI lookup, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 45 formats a target path template in inline Markdown. It does not execute a command or interpolate untrusted input.
Line 47 opens a Markdown template block that shows what a new SKILL.md should contain. The fenced content is sample documentation, not active code.
Line 60 uses Markdown to link to a sibling shared skill inside a template. This is a documentation reference and not command execution.
Line 64 contains an escaped code fence inside the sample Markdown template. It is intended to teach template formatting, not to execute shell code.
Line 71 contains an escaped closing code fence in the sample template. It has no execution semantics.
Line 77 formats a placeholder scope name in a permissions table. This is static documentation, not executable content.
Line 78 closes the outer Markdown template block. It is not a Ruby or shell execution pattern.
Line 83 documents the legitimate lark-cli auth login command required for this tool. It is an explicit user-facing prerequisite, not hidden execution or command injection.
Line 39 uses ../ only in a Markdown link to a bundled sibling skill. There is no file read, write, or user-controlled path traversal behavior.
Line 60 uses ../ in a Markdown reference to the shared sibling skill. It is a static documentation link, not filesystem access.
Line 70 is a placeholder comment in a workflow template about reusing a previous step identifier. It does not request host, account, network, or system reconnaissance.

The file is readable Markdown front matter and Chinese documentation. The entropy heuristic appears to be triggered by multilingual prose and Markdown structure, not binary, encrypted, or obfuscated content.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable ways to package Lark API work into agent-ready instructions. This skill provides a template, research flow, and safety checklist for building reusable lark-cli skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains core lark-cli command forms for registered APIs, shortcuts, raw OpenAPI calls, and schema lookup.
Provides a research workflow for finding services, resources, methods, parameters, and permission scopes.
Supplies a SKILL.md template with metadata, command sections, permissions, and required tool declarations.
Shows how to document single-step and multi-step Lark API workflows with data handoff between steps.
Recommends authentication, write confirmation, dry-run previews, rollback notes, and parallelization guidance.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and authenticated before generated skills can run Lark operations.
Does not create files by itself; the agent or user must write the final SKILL.md content.
Depends on available Lark API permissions and workspace scopes for successful execution.
Raw OpenAPI calls require careful parameter validation and user confirmation for write actions.

use_cases.title: Package Repeated Admin Tasks
use_cases.description: Turn repeated Lark workspace tasks into reusable skill instructions with clear commands and permissions.

use_cases.title: Build Team Automation Skills
use_cases.description: Create shared skills that combine Lark API calls, shortcuts, and multi-step data handoff.

use_cases.title: Document Lark API Workflows
use_cases.description: Capture required scopes, parameters, confirmation points, and rollback notes for new Lark integrations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one Lark operation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lark CLI skill for one repeated task. Include the trigger description, required command, needed scope, and user confirmation step.

prompt_templates.title: Research an API First
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request when the correct Lark API is unknown.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the Lark API needed for this task, then draft a reusable skill with the command path, parameters, permissions, and safety notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with data passing between API calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-step Lark CLI skill for this workflow. Show each step, the data passed forward, failure handling, rollback notes, and required scopes.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Generated Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before sharing a team skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Lark CLI skill for trigger quality, command correctness, permissions, write safety, dry-run support, and missing rollback guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for finding meeting rooms by floor.
output_examples.output: A concise skill draft with a clear trigger, room search command, required permissions, parameter notes, and read-only safety guidance.

output_examples.input: Turn a two-step approval update into a reusable skill.
output: A workflow outline that identifies the first response value to store.
A second step that uses that value in the next Lark operation.
Permission, confirmation, rollback, and failure-handling notes.

output_examples.input: Review whether my Lark skill is ready to share.
output_examples.output: A structured review covering trigger wording, command shape, scope accuracy, write safeguards, and missing operational notes.

best_practices: Define the skill trigger with specific task words and a clear usage scenario.
List exact Lark scopes and require explicit confirmation before write operations.
Document data handoff, failure handling, rollback behavior, and dry-run options for multi-step flows.
anti_patterns: Do not create broad skills that call raw OpenAPI endpoints without naming the task and permission scope.
Do not omit confirmation steps for actions that create, update, delete, or notify users.
Do not hide required authentication, workspace domain, or permission assumptions from the generated skill.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you draft reusable Lark CLI skills that describe commands, parameters, scopes, and safety rules for Lark API tasks.

faq.question: Does it run Lark commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples for agents or users to follow with lark-cli.

faq.question: Do I need lark-cli installed?
faq.answer: Yes. Generated skills expect lark-cli to be available and authenticated for the target Lark workspace.

faq.question: Can it use APIs that are not registered in lark-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to research native Lark OpenAPI paths and call them through the raw API command form.

faq.question: How does it handle permissions?
faq.answer: It prompts the skill author to list required scopes and document authentication before the workflow runs.

faq.question: Is it suitable for write operations?
faq.answer: Yes, when the generated skill includes explicit confirmation, minimal scopes, dry-run checks, and rollback guidance.
